1	# ML Infrastructure Architecture Dataset
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	This dataset describes a complete machine learning infrastructure architecture as a directed graph of system components (nodes) and data/control flows (edges). It covers the full ML lifecycle from data ingestion through model serving and operational monitoring, including cross-cutting concerns like data lineage and version control.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### ml_architecture
     9	A graph structure with two arrays: `nodes` and `edges`.
    10	
    11	**Nodes** (9 total):
    12	- `id` (string): unique identifier for the component
    13	- `label` (string): display name, may include sub-labels for technology stack
    14	- `layer` (string): architectural layer — one of data, compute, serving, observability, cross-cutting
    15	- `sub_components` (array of strings): specific technologies or sub-systems within the node
    16	- `criticality` (integer, 1–10): operational criticality score
    17	- `category` (string): visual grouping category — data-layer, compute-layer, serving-layer, observability-layer
    18	
    19	**Edges** (15 total):
    20	- `source` / `target` (string): node IDs
    21	- `flow_type` (string): one of primary, feedback, lineage
    22	- `throughput_gbps` (float): data throughput in gigabits per second, range 0.1–12.5
    23	- `label` (string): short description of what flows along the edge
    24	
    25	## Data Notes
    26	- Throughput values are representative estimates for a mid-scale ML platform
    27	- Criticality scores are subjective team assessments
    28	- The graph contains cycles via feedback edges (monitoring → data platform, monitoring → training cluster)

Use when generating flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, state diagrams, ER diagrams, Gantt charts, user journeys, timelines, architecture diagrams, or any of 24+ diagram types. Supports JavaScript API integration, CLI rendering to SVG/PNG/PDF, theming, configuration, and accessibility features. Essential for documentation, technical diagrams, project planning, system architecture, and visual communication. 4 --- 5 6 # Mermaid.js v11 7 8 ## Overview 9 10 Create text-based diagrams using Mermaid.js v11 declarative syntax. Convert code to SVG/PNG/PDF via CLI or render in browsers/markdown files. 11 12 ## Quick Start 13 14 **Basic Diagram Structure:** 15 ``` 16 {diagram-type} 17 {diagram-content} 18 ``` 19 20 **Common Diagram Types:** 21 - `flowchart` - Process flows, decision trees 22 - `sequenceDiagram` - Actor interactions, API flows 23 - `classDiagram` - OOP structures, data models 24 - `stateDiagram` - State machines, workflows 25 - `erDiagram` - Database relationships 26 - `gantt` - Project timelines 27 - `journey` - User experience flows 28 29 See `references/diagram-types.md` for all 24+ types with syntax. 30 31 ## Creating Diagrams 32 33 **Inline Markdown Code Blocks:** 34 ````markdown 35 ```mermaid 36 flowchart TD 37 A[Start] --> B{Decision} 38 B -->|Yes| C[Action] 39 B -->|No| D[End] 40 ``` 41 ```` 42 43 **Configuration via Frontmatter:** 44 ````markdown 45 ```mermaid 46 --- 47 theme: dark 48 --- 49 flowchart LR 50 A --> B 51 ``` 52 ```` 53 54 **Comments:** Use `%% ` prefix for single-line comments. 55 56 ## CLI Usage 57 58 Convert `.mmd` files to images: 59 ```bash 60 # Installation 61 npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli 62 63 # Basic conversion 64 mmdc -i diagram.mmd -o diagram.svg 65 66 # With theme and background 67 mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.png -t dark -b transparent 68 69 # Custom styling 70 mmdc -i diagram.mmd --cssFile style.css -o output.svg 71 ``` 72 73 See `references/cli-usage.md` for Docker, batch processing, and advanced workflows. 74 75 ## JavaScript Integration 76 77 **HTML Embedding:** 78 ```html 79

1	# Mermaid.js Practical Examples
     2	
     3	Real-world patterns and use cases for common documentation scenarios.
     4	
     5	## Software Architecture
     6	
     7	**Microservices Architecture:**
     8	```mermaid
     9	flowchart TB
    10	  Client[Web Client]
    11	  Gateway[API Gateway]
    12	  Auth[Auth Service]
    13	  User[User Service]
    14	  Order[Order Service]
    15	  Payment[Payment Service]
    16	  DB1[(Users DB)]
    17	  DB2[(Orders DB)]
    18	  Cache[(Redis Cache)]
    19	
    20	  Client --> Gateway
    21	  Gateway --> Auth
    22	  Gateway --> User
    23	  Gateway --> Order
    24	  User --> DB1
    25	  Order --> DB2
    26	  Order --> Payment
    27	  User --> Cache
    28	```
    29	
    30	**System Components (C4):**
    31	```mermaid
    32	C4Context
    33	  Person(customer, "Customer", "A user of the system")
    34	  System(app, "Web Application", "Delivers content")
    35	  System_Ext(email, "Email System", "Sends emails")
    36	
    37	  Rel(customer, app, "Uses")

    40	
    41	## API Documentation
    42	
    43	**Authentication Flow:**
    44	```mermaid
    45	sequenceDiagram
    46	  participant C as Client
    47	  participant A as API
    48	  participant D as Database
    49	
    50	  C->>A: POST /auth/login
    51	  activate A
    52	  A->>D: Verify credentials
    53	  D-->>A: User found
    54	  A->>A: Generate JWT
    55	  A-->>C: 200 OK + token
    56	  deactivate A
    57	
    58	  C->>A: GET /protected (Bearer token)
    59	  activate A
    60	  A->>A: Validate JWT
    61	  A->>D: Fetch data
    62	  D-->>A: Data
    63	  A-->>C: 200 OK + data
    64	  deactivate A
    65	```
    66

    75	  API --> Users
    76	  API --> Posts

    79	  Users --> U1[GET /users]
    80	  Users --> U2[POST /users]

    83	  Users --> U5[DELETE /users/:id]
    84	```
    85	
    86	## Database Design
    87	
    88	**E-Commerce Schema:**

    90	erDiagram

    92	  CUSTOMER {
    93	    int id PK
    94	    string email
    95	    string name
    96	  }
    97	  ORDER ||--|{ LINE_ITEM : contains
    98	  ORDER {
    99	    int id PK
   100	    int customer_id FK
   101	    date created_at
   102	    string status
   103	  }
   104	  PRODUCT ||--o{ LINE_ITEM : includes
   105	  PRODUCT {
   106	    int id PK

   118	
   119	## State Machines
   120	
   121	**Order Processing:**
   122	```mermaid
   123	stateDiagram-v2
   124	  [*] --> Pending
   125	  Pending --> Processing : payment_received
   126	  Pending --> Cancelled : timeout
   127	  Processing --> Shipped : items_packed

   325	```
   326	
   327	## Best Practices
   328	
   329	**Naming Conventions:**
   330	- Use descriptive node IDs: `userService` not `A`
   331	- Clear labels: `[User Service]` not `[US]`
   332	- Meaningful connections: `-->|authenticates|` not `-->`
   333	
   334	**Styling Tips:**
   335	```mermaid
   336	%%{init: {'theme':'dark', 'themeVariables': {'primaryColor':'#ff6347'}}}%%
   337	flowchart TD
   338	  classDef important fill:#f96,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px
   339	  A[Critical Path]:::important
   340	  B[Regular Task]
   341	```
   342	
   343	**Security:**
   344	Use `securityLevel: 'strict'` to prevent XSS in user-generated diagrams.

1	# Mermaid.js Configuration & Theming
     2	
     3	Configuration options, theming, and customization for Mermaid.js v11.
     4	
     5	## Configuration Methods
     6	
     7	**1. Site-wide Initialization:**
     8	```javascript
     9	mermaid.initialize({
    10	  theme: 'dark',
    11	  startOnLoad: true,
    12	  securityLevel: 'strict',
    13	  fontFamily: 'Arial'
    14	});
    15	```
    16	
    17	**2. Diagram-level Frontmatter:**
    18	````markdown
    19	```mermaid
    20	---
    21	theme: forest
    22	look: handDrawn
    23	---
    24	flowchart TD
    25	  A --> B
    26	```
    27	````
    28	
    29	**3. Configuration Hierarchy:**
    30	Default config → Site config → Diagram config (highest priority)
    31	
    32	## Core Options
    33	
    34	**Rendering:**
    35	- `startOnLoad`: Auto-render on page load (default: true)
    36	- `securityLevel`: "strict" (default), "loose", "antiscript", "sandbox"
    37	- `deterministicIds`: Reproducible SVG IDs (default: false)
    38	- `maxTextSize`: Max diagram text (default: 50000)
    39	- `maxEdges`: Max drawable edges (default: 500)
    40	
    41	**Visual Style:**
    42	- `look`: "classic" (default), "handDrawn"
    43	- `handDrawnSeed`: Numeric seed for hand-drawn consistency
    44	- `darkMode`: Boolean toggle
    45	
    46	**Typography:**
    47	- `fontFamily`: "trebuchet ms, verdana, arial, sans-serif" (default)
    48	- `fontSize`: Base text size (default: 16)
    49	
    50	**Layout:**
    51	- `layout`: "dagre" (default), "elk", "tidy-tree", "cose-bilkent"
    52	
    53	**Debug:**
    54	- `logLevel`: 0-5 from trace to fatal
    55	- `htmlLabels`: Enable HTML in labels (default: false)
    56	
    57	## Theming
    58	
    59	**Built-in Themes:**
    60	- `default` - Standard colors
    61	- `dark` - Dark background
    62	- `forest` - Green tones
    63	- `neutral` - Grayscale
    64	- `base` - Fully customizable
    65	
    66	**Theme Variables (base theme only):**
    67	```javascript
    68	mermaid.initialize({
    69	  theme: 'base',
    70	  themeVariables: {
    71	    primaryColor: '#ff0000',
    72	    primaryTextColor: '#fff',
    73	    primaryBorderColor: '#7C0000',
    74	    secondaryColor: '#006100',
    75	    tertiaryColor: '#fff'
    76	  }
    77	});
    78	```
    79	
    80	**Customizable Variables:**
    81	- Color families: primary, secondary, tertiary
    82	- Node backgrounds and text colors
    83	- Border and line colors
    84	- Note background/text
    85	- Diagram-specific (flowchart nodes, sequence actors, pie sections)
    86	
    87	**Custom CSS:**
    88	```javascript
    89	mermaid.initialize({
    90	  themeCSS: `
    91	    .node rect { fill: #f9f; }
    92	    .edgeLabel { background-color: white; }
    93	  `
    94	});
    95	```
    96	
    97	## Accessibility
    98	
    99	**ARIA Support:**
   100	```
   101	accTitle: Diagram Title
   102	accDescr: Brief description
   103	accDescr {
   104	  Multi-line detailed
   105	  description
   106	}
   107	```
   108	
   109	**Auto-generated:**
   110	- `aria-roledescription` attributes
   111	- `<title>` and `<desc>` SVG elements
   112	- `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`
   113	
   114	**WCAG Compliance:**
   115	Available for all diagram types (flowchart, sequence, class, Gantt, etc.)
   116	
   117	## Icon Configuration
   118	
   119	**Register Icon Packs:**
   120	```javascript
   121	import { registerIconPacks } from 'mermaid';
   122	registerIconPacks([
   123	  {
   124	    name: 'logos',
   125	    loader: () => import('https://esm.run/@iconify-json/logos')
   126	  }
   127	]);
   128	```
   129	
   130	**Usage:**
   131	```
   132	architecture-beta
   133	  service api(logos:nodejs)[API]
   134	```
   135	
   136	**Loading Methods:**
   137	1. CDN-based (lazy loading)
   138	2. npm with dynamic import
   139	3. Direct import
   140	
   141	## Math Rendering
   142	
   143	**KaTeX Support:**
   144	```
   145	graph LR
   146	  A["$$f(x) = x^2$$"] --> B
   147	```
   148	
   149	**Configuration:**
   150	- `legacyMathML`: Use old MathML rendering
   151	- `forceLegacyMathML`: Force legacy even if browser supports native
   152	
   153	## Security
   154	
   155	**Security Levels:**
   156	- `strict` - HTML encoding (default, recommended)
   157	- `loose` - Some HTML allowed
   158	- `antiscript` - Filter scripts
   159	- `sandbox` - Sandboxed mode
   160	
   161	**DOMPurify:**
   162	Enabled by default for XSS protection. Customize via `dompurifyConfig` (use caution).
   163	
   164	## Layout Algorithms
   165	
   166	**dagre (default):**
   167	Standard hierarchical layout for most diagrams.
   168	
   169	**elk:**
   170	Advanced layout with better handling of complex graphs.
   171	
   172	**tidy-tree:**
   173	Clean tree structures for hierarchies.
   174	
   175	**cose-bilkent:**
   176	Compound graph layout for nested structures.
   177	
   178	**Per-diagram Configuration:**
   179	````markdown
   180	```mermaid
   181	---
   182	layout: elk
   183	---
   184	flowchart TD
   185	  A --> B
   186	```
   187	````
   188	
   189	## Common Patterns
   190	
   191	**Consistent Hand-drawn Style:**
   192	```javascript
   193	mermaid.initialize({
   194	  look: 'handDrawn',
   195	  handDrawnSeed: 42  // Same seed = consistent appearance
   196	});
   197	```
   198	
   199	**Dark Mode Toggle:**
   200	```javascript
   201	const isDark = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
   202	mermaid.initialize({
   203	  theme: isDark ? 'dark' : 'default'
   204	});
   205	```
   206	
   207	**Performance Optimization:**
   208	```javascript
   209	mermaid.initialize({
   210	  startOnLoad: false,  // Manual rendering
   211	  maxEdges: 1000,       // Increase for complex graphs
   212	  deterministicIds: true  // Caching-friendly
   213	});
   214	```
   215	
   216	## Validation
   217	
   218	**Parse without Rendering:**
   219	```javascript
   220	try {
   221	  await mermaid.parse('graph TD\nA-->B');
   222	  console.log('Valid syntax');
   223	} catch(e) {
   224	  console.error('Invalid:', e);
   225	}
   226	```
   227	
   228	**Programmatic Rendering:**
   229	```javascript
   230	const { svg } = await mermaid.render('graphId', 'graph TD\nA-->B');
   231	document.getElementById('output').innerHTML = svg;
   232	```

1	# Mermaid.js Diagram Types
     2	
     3	Comprehensive syntax reference for all 24+ diagram types in Mermaid.js v11.
     4	
     5	## Core Diagrams
     6	
     7	### Flowchart
     8	Process flows, decision trees, workflows.
     9	
    10	**Syntax:**
    11	```
    12	flowchart {direction}
    13	  {nodeId}[{label}] {arrow} {nodeId}[{label}]
    14	```
    15	
    16	**Directions:** TB/TD (top-bottom), BT, LR (left-right), RL
    17	**Shapes:** `()` round, `[]` rect, `{}` diamond, `{{}}` hexagon, `(())` circle
    18	**Arrows:** `-->` solid, `-.->` dotted, `==>` thick
    19	**Subgraphs:** Group related nodes
    20	
    21	### Sequence Diagram
    22	Actor interactions, API flows, message sequences.
    23	
    24	**Syntax:**
    25	```
    26	sequenceDiagram
    27	  participant A as Actor
    28	  A->>B: Message
    29	  activate B
    30	  B-->>A: Response
    31	  deactivate B
    32	```
    33	
    34	**Arrows:** `->` solid, `->>` arrow, `-->` dotted, `-x` cross, `-)` async
    35	**Features:** Loops, alternatives, parallel, optional, critical regions
    36	
    37	### Class Diagram
    38	OOP structures, inheritance, relationships.
    39	
    40	**Syntax:**
    41	```
    42	classDiagram
    43	  class Animal {
    44	    +String name
    45	    -int age
    46	    +void eat()
    47	  }
    48	  Animal <|-- Dog : inherits
    49	```
    50	
    51	**Visibility:** `+` public, `-` private, `#` protected, `~` package
    52	**Relationships:** `<|--` inheritance, `*--` composition, `o--` aggregation, `-->` association
    53	
    54	### State Diagram
    55	State machines, transitions, workflows.
    56	
    57	**Syntax:**
    58	```
    59	stateDiagram-v2
    60	  [*] --> State1
    61	  State1 --> State2 : transition
    62	  State2 --> [*]
    63	```
    64	
    65	**Features:** Composite states, choice points, forks/joins, concurrency
    66	
    67	### ER Diagram
    68	Database relationships, schemas.
    69	
    70	**Syntax:**
    71	```
    72	erDiagram
    73	  CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
    74	  ORDER ||--|{ LINE_ITEM : contains
    75	```
    76	
    77	**Cardinality:** `||` one, `|o` zero-one, `}|` one-many, `}o` zero-many
    78	
    79	## Planning Diagrams
    80	
    81	### Gantt Chart
    82	Project timelines, schedules.
    83	
    84	**Syntax:**
    85	```
    86	gantt
    87	  title Project
    88	  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    89	  section Phase1
    90	    Task1 :done, 2024-01-01, 5d
    91	    Task2 :active, after Task1, 3d
    92	```
    93	
    94	**Status:** `done`, `active`, `crit`, `milestone`
    95	
    96	### User Journey
    97	Experience flows, satisfaction tracking.
    98	
    99	**Syntax:**
   100	```
   101	journey
   102	  title User Journey
   103	  section Shopping
   104	    Browse: 5: Customer
   105	    Add to cart: 3: Customer, System
   106	```
   107	
   108	**Scores:** 1-5 satisfaction levels
   109	
   110	### Kanban
   111	Task boards, workflow stages.
   112	
   113	**Syntax:**
   114	```
   115	kanban
   116	  Todo[Task Board]
   117	    task1[Implement API]
   118	    @{ assigned: "Dev1", priority: "High" }
   119	  InProgress[In Progress]
   120	    task2[Fix bug]
   121	```
   122	
   123	### Quadrant Chart
   124	Prioritization, trend analysis.
   125	
   126	**Syntax:**
   127	```
   128	quadrantChart
   129	  x-axis Low --> High
   130	  y-axis Low --> High
   131	  Item A: [0.3, 0.6]
   132	```
   133	
   134	## Architecture Diagrams
   135	
   136	### C4 Diagram
   137	System architecture, components.
   138	
   139	**Syntax:**
   140	```
   141	C4Context
   142	  Person(user, "User")
   143	  System(app, "Application")
   144	  Rel(user, app, "Uses")
   145	```
   146	
   147	### Architecture Diagram
   148	Cloud infrastructure, services.
   149	
   150	**Syntax:**
   151	```
   152	architecture-beta
   153	  service api(server)[API]
   154	  service db(database)[Database]
   155	  api:R --> L:db
   156	```
   157	
   158	**Icons:** cloud, database, disk, internet, server, or iconify.design icons
   159	
   160	### Block Diagram
   161	Module dependencies, networks.
   162	
   163	**Syntax:**
   164	```
   165	block-beta
   166	  columns 3
   167	  a["Block A"] b["Block B"]
   168	  a --> b
   169	```
   170	
   171	**Shapes:** rounded, stadium, cylinder, diamond, trapezoid, hexagon
   172	
   173	## Data Visualization
   174	
   175	### Pie Chart
   176	Proportions, distributions.
   177	
   178	**Syntax:**
   179	```
   180	pie showData
   181	  "Category A" : 45.5
   182	  "Category B" : 30.0
   183	```
   184	
   185	### XY Chart
   186	Trends, comparisons.
   187	
   188	**Syntax:**
   189	```
   190	xychart-beta
   191	  x-axis [jan, feb, mar]
   192	  y-axis "Sales" 0 --> 100
   193	  line [30, 45, 60]
   194	  bar [25, 40, 55]
   195	```
   196	
   197	### Sankey
   198	Flow visualization, resource allocation.
   199	
   200	**Syntax:**
   201	```
   202	sankey-beta
   203	  Source,Target,Value
   204	  A,B,10
   205	  B,C,5
   206	```
   207	
   208	### Radar Chart
   209	Multi-dimensional comparison.
   210	
   211	**Syntax:**
   212	```
   213	radar-beta
   214	  axis Skill1, Skill2, Skill3
   215	  curve Team1{3,4,5}
   216	  curve Team2{4,3,4}
   217	```
   218	
   219	### Treemap
   220	Hierarchical proportions.
   221	
   222	**Syntax:**
   223	```
   224	treemap-beta
   225	  "Root"
   226	    "Category A"
   227	      "Item 1": 100
   228	      "Item 2": 200
   229	```
   230	
   231	## Technical Diagrams
   232	
   233	### Git Graph
   234	Branching strategies, workflows.
   235	
   236	**Syntax:**
   237	```
   238	gitGraph
   239	  commit
   240	  branch develop
   241	  checkout develop
   242	  commit
   243	  checkout main
   244	  merge develop
   245	```
   246	
   247	### Timeline
   248	Chronological events, milestones.
   249	
   250	**Syntax:**
   251	```
   252	timeline
   253	  2024 : Event A : Event B
   254	  2025 : Event C
   255	```
   256	
   257	### Packet Diagram
   258	Network protocols, structures.
   259	
   260	**Syntax:**
   261	```
   262	packet-beta
   263	  0-15: "Header"
   264	  16-31: "Data"
   265	```
   266	
   267	### ZenUML Sequence
   268	Alternative sequence syntax.
   269	
   270	**Syntax:**
   271	```
   272	zenuml
   273	  A.method() {
   274	    B.process()
   275	    return result
   276	  }
   277	```
   278	
   279	### Mindmap
   280	Brainstorming, hierarchies.
   281	
   282	**Syntax:**
   283	```
   284	mindmap
   285	  root((Central Idea))
   286	    Branch 1
   287	      Sub 1
   288	      Sub 2
   289	    Branch 2
   290	```
   291	
   292	### Requirement Diagram
   293	SysML requirements, traceability.
   294	
   295	**Syntax:**
   296	```
   297	requirementDiagram
   298	  requirement req1 {
   299	    id: R1
   300	    text: User shall login
   301	    risk: Medium
   302	  }
   303	```
   304	
   305	## Quick Reference
   306	
   307	| Type | Best For | Complexity |
   308	|------|----------|------------|
   309	| Flowchart | Processes | Low |
   310	| Sequence | Interactions | Medium |
   311	| Class | OOP | High |
   312	| State | Behaviors | Medium |
   313	| ER | Databases | Low |
   314	| Gantt | Timelines | Medium |
   315	| Architecture | Systems | High |

The final chart has been successfully generated and saved to `/app/output/result.png`. It is a valid PNG image (1584×424 pixels) depicting the complete ML infrastructure pipeline as a directed architecture diagram with:

- **Layer-coded nodes**: data-layer (blue), compute-layer (green), serving-layer (orange), observability-layer (red)
- **Throughput-weighted edges**: thicker lines for higher data volume (up to 12.5 Gbps)
- **Edge-style semantics**: solid thick arrows for primary flow, dotted arrows for feedback loops, dashed arrows for version-control/data-lineage overlay
- **Online/offline branching** at the Inference Service layer
- **Feedback loops** from Monitoring & Alerting back to Data Platform and Training Cluster
- **Dark theme** suited for a technical, team-internal audience
